Title: Two-Factor Authentication Setup
FAQ: How do I set up two-factor authentication?

Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of security to your account. To enable 2FA, go to Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication and click Enable. We support authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy) and SMS verification. Authenticator apps are recommended over SMS for stronger security. After enabling 2FA, you will be prompted for a verification code at each login.
--- End Document 1 ---

Title: Analysis of variance
he effects of multiple factors has a complication. In a 3-way ANOVA with factors x, y and z, the ANOVA model includes terms for the main effects (x, y, z) and terms for interactions (xy, xz, yz, xyz). 
All terms require hypothesis tests. The proliferation of interaction terms increases the risk that some hypothesis test will produce a false positive by chance. Fortunately, experience says that high order interactions are rare.
--- End Document 3 ---

Title: Security Policy
Information Security Policy

All users and employees must adhere to the following security guidelines. Passwords must be at least 12 characters and include uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols. Passwords must be changed every 90 days. Never reuse the last 5 passwords. Two-factor authentication is mandatory for all accounts with administrative privileges. Users must lock their workstations when away from their desks.
--- End Document 4 ---

final_answer:
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is a security measure that requires users to provide two or more credentials to access a system or application. This adds an extra layer of security by making it more difficult for unauthorized individuals to gain access. MFA typically involves using a combination of something the user knows (e.g., a password or PIN), something the user has (e.g., a smartphone or a physical token), and something the user is (e.g., biometric information such as a fingerprint or facial recognition). By requiring multiple credentials, MFA makes it much more difficult for attackers to successfully authenticate and gain access to sensitive information or systems.
